decision: Use PR preview as staging for northvalleyintel.com.
reason: Production deploys only from main; user requested staging validation before production.

decision: Email the teaser PDF instead of rendering the report live.
reason: The complete report should remain a paid service and the site should capture qualified interest.
User-provided contact@northvalleyinte.com appears to be a typo for the known Northvalley domain.

decision: Host the MCP endpoint at https://northvalleyintel.com/mcp on the apex domain as a Cloudflare Pages Function.
reason: Avoids creating a second subdomain that can sit pending — the exact failure this phase is closing. OpenAI's domain-verification challenge is fetched from the host root with any subpath stripped, so apex keeps server and token on one host. The medinaclean build reached the same conclusion from the other direction.

decision: Implement /mcp as a Cloudflare Pages Function in functions/, not a Next.js route handler.
reason: This project is output: export, a fully static build with no Next route handlers. Pages Functions already receive a Web Request and return a Web Response, which is the exact shape WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport targets.

decision: Use Cloudflare KV as the durable throttle store for the MCP write path.
reason: Northvalley stores nothing today — the intake path is Pages Function straight to Resend — so Medina's $0 Supabase row-count throttle has no analogue. KV is the simplest durable counter on the existing platform and survives across Worker isolates. Founder selected it on 2026-08-05, accepting one new binding.

decision: Ship the MCP endpoint anonymous, with no auth.
reason: All three tools (list_services, request_assessment, request_consult) are anonymous submission and none returns user-specific data. OAuth is required only when tools expose user-specific data. Matches the medinaclean precedent. Founder selected on 2026-08-05.

decision: Publish the Medina Clean client card under business-name-only consent.
reason: Founder confirmed consent scope on 2026-08-05 as business name only: no personal name for the owner and no booking screenshot. The end-to-end booking claim was not separately affirmed, so it is held until explicitly confirmed.

decision: Keep the Cobb/Paulding/Douglas focus out of the MCP tool surface entirely.
reason: The county focus is an input to the lead-growth analysis inside the assessment, not a boundary on who Northvalley works with. Northvalley works with clients anywhere in the US, so a service-area gate would wrongly turn callers away. Location is collected as a field on request_assessment, never as an eligibility check.

decision: Naming Rosa in Medina Clean case-study content is consented.
reason: Founder confirmed on 2026-08-05 that Rosa's consent is held in a text message. This reconciles the earlier business-name-only answer with the fact that /case-studies/medina-clean/rosas-story was already live in production and names her across seven files. Consent evidence lives outside the repo; keep the text on file.

decision: Never fall back to a shared Resend sandbox sender on any customer-facing path.
reason: onboarding@resend.dev only delivers to the Resend account owner, so a teaser addressed to a prospect is rejected while the admin copy still lands. The failure then reads as success from inside Northvalley. The teaser now throws rather than attempting a send from any @resend.dev address.

decision: A failed teaser delivery must email Northvalley, not only console.warn.
reason: console.warn in a Cloudflare Worker is visible only to someone tailing logs at that moment. The requester has already been promised the teaser, so a silent failure strands them. The alert is deliberately addressed to the Northvalley inbox because that path still works when the sending domain is misconfigured.
